source.title: Algebraicity of higher Green functions at a CM point
readSections: Published version (open access, CC BY 4.0), read in full on 2026-09-22 (PDF SHA-256 1381077a24dee11d613c5b5f437f281080e89d26bb900fc6e1134360b883e163). Statement numbers and pages are the published ones.
arXiv v2 TeX source (SHA-256 7d35388932a5da5f92bf7782c7c79048d3aac1a384beddd9ba96f904bd198271) was used as a reading aid; it matches the published text up to layout.

Checked in detail: Example 2.1, Lemma 2.2, the proof of Proposition 2.6, Lemmas 2.8–2.9 (with the counterexample of E2 verified numerically), Lemmas 3.2–3.3, Proposition 3.4, Theorem 4.1 and Proposition 4.2 (whence E6), Lemma 4.6, Proposition 4.8, the proof of Theorem 4.10, the reduction and weight bookkeeping in §5.1, and the linear algebra at the end of §5.2. Results of Bruinier (2012), Bruinier–Yang (2011), Bruinier–Ehlen–Yang (2021) and Bruinier–Kudla–Yang (2012) were used as quoted.

Independent review 2026-09-23: all 44 pages of the published article read, including all definitions, proofs and references. arXiv v2 inspected at selected operator, compactification, local-singularity and §5 proof locators, not a new full line-by-line version diff. Input reading is recorded separately; full-paper claims for cited references are not made.

summary: Independent review of all 39 original items and the full published paper. Correct the operator orientation and quotient-harmonic condition, Gaussian and Green normalizations, inverse-action singularity criterion, Stokes measure and CM evaluation domain. Split omitted carriers and proof steps; import classical Hilbert forms from B4 and coordinate the shared BEY Part II. Explicit boundary regularity, primary-source and normalization obligations keep the extraction partial. The higher-lift half-factor is now derived from BEY Proposition 4.7; remaining G3 concerns the regularization/application check. Upstream StableReduction Layer 4 already owns blowups.

items.name: Elliptic holomorphic modular and cusp forms
items.statement: For a subgroup Γ of GL₂(R) and integral weight k, ModularForm Γ k consists of slash-invariant functions on the upper half-plane, holomorphic there and bounded at every cusp; CuspForm requires vanishing at every cusp. Specialize to SL₂(Z).

items.name: Harmonic Maass forms, the lowering operator and the ξ-operator
items.statement: For the specified finite Weil representation, a harmonic weak Maass form of weight k is a smooth slash-invariant function annihilated by Δ_k which, at each cusp, differs from a finite holomorphic Fourier principal part by O(exp(−εv)). Use R_k=2i∂τ+k/v, L_k=−2iv²∂conjτ and Δ_k=−R_{k−2}L_k. Its holomorphic/nonholomorphic Fourier decomposition and antilinear ξ_k=2iv^k conjugate(∂conjτ) give the cusp shadow of weight 2−k. Merely allowing arbitrary exponential growth does not guarantee a cusp shadow.

items.name: Siegel theta kernels and definite theta series
items.statement: For an even O_F-lattice L in V of signature ((p₁,q₁),(n+2,0),...), use φ∞=v₁^(q₁/2)e(Q(λ_z⊥)τ₁+Q(λ_z)conj(τ₁)) times the positive Gaussians at the other embeddings. Sum φ_μ(h⁻¹λ)φ∞ over λ∈V(F) and μ∈L′/L to obtain Θ_L of weight ((p₁−q₁)/2,n/2+1,...), representation ρ_L. Prove convergence and the adelic lattice-change identity (3.11). For definite first signature omit z and write θ_L; for P∈U_F⁺ it is scalar-valued, holomorphic, of parallel weight rank(P)/2.

items.name: Baily–Borel compactification of Hilbert modular varieties and ampleness of the Hodge line
items.statement: X^BB = Proj of the ring of Hilbert modular forms is a normal projective scheme obtained by adding finitely many cusps, and the determinant of the Hodge bundle (weight (1, …, 1)) is ample on it.
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V2 plans the Baily–Borel theorem and minimal compactification.

items.name: Smooth toroidal compactifications as normalized blow-ups (AMRT IV Thm. 2.2) and Koecher's principle
items.statement: At neat level and for a smooth projective admissible fan, the Hilbert toroidal compactification is smooth projective and maps to the minimal compactification as the normalization of a blowup in a coherent cusp-supported ideal (AMRT IV.2.2). Koecher extension holds in Hilbert degree >1 with the relevant coefficient hypotheses; in degree one retain the cusp growth condition.
items.note: Import compactification from C2/C6 and automorphic extensions from B3/B4. Do not infer smooth boundary extension of arbitrary bounded real-analytic functions, or pullback of every coherent minimal extension; E17 and G1.

items.name: Dolbeault exact sequence with vector-bundle coefficients
items.statement: On a compact complex manifold, with E′=ker(∂̄:E^{0,1}→E^{0,2}), the sequence 0→O→E^{0,0}→E′→0 is exact. Tensor with a holomorphic vector bundle; the smooth middle sheaf is fine, so vanishing of H¹ of the bundle gives surjectivity on global ∂̄-closed (0,1)-forms.
items.note: ComplexComparisonPartII C1 plans analytic coherent cohomology with ∂̄-problems and 'the analytic vanishing and generation theorem'; C2 plans projective GAGA.

items.name: Canonical models of GSpin Shimura varieties and Shimura reciprocity at CM points
items.statement: X_K = H(Q)\D × H(Q̂)/K for H = Res_{F/Q} GSpin_V has a canonical model over σ_1(F) (Shih), and Gal(E_W^ab/E_W) acts on the CM points of Z(W, h) through class field theory (Shimura reciprocity; AGHMP18 §§3.1, 5.3).
items.note: ShimuraVarieties V4 plans canonical models and the special-point reciprocity condition, and V6 plans Hodge and abelian type (Res GSpin is of abelian type).

items.name: CM points on X_0(N) and their fields of definition
items.statement: CM points z of discriminant d on X_0(1) are defined over the ring class field H_z of Q(√d), and Gal(H_z/Q(√d)) acts on them through the class group of the order.
items.note: HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.1 plans CM points, compatible parametrizations and descent to ring class fields.

items.name: Existence of definite integral unimodular O_F-lattices with prescribed signs
items.statement: For each totally real F and each choice of definite sign at its real embeddings, there exists a nonzero even integral O_F-lattice self-dual for its O_F-valued bilinear pairing with those signatures; rank divisible by 8 suffices. This is the particular consequence of Chang Satz 1 used by Li, not a claim about every quadratic space of that dimension.
items.note: Chang full article not acquired: the download rendered its subscription landing page. Bogo–Li Proposition 2.1 confirms the quoted use but does not reproduce the local criterion. G2 requires the precise criterion and proof, including dyadic conditions.

items.name: Proposition 2.6: totally positive Z-unimodular O-lattices exist
items.statement: For any totally real field F, the semigroup U_F^+ of non-trivial, totally positive definite, even Z-unimodular O-lattices (L′ = L for Q_Z = tr_{F/Q} Q) is non-empty.
items.note: The dual calculation was checked independently: with δQ on aL, trace-integrality is equivalent to pairing with a⁻¹L into O, hence (aL)′=aL#=aL. The existence inputs remain G2.

items.name: Mass-normalized definite theta average and Hecke Eisenstein expansion
items.statement: For a totally positive even Z-unimodular O_F-lattice P of rank 2k in the convergent range, normalize Haar measure on the compact orthogonal adelic quotient to total mass one. Its theta integral is the normalized Hecke Eisenstein series E_{F,k}, whose constant coefficient is 1. On a finite genus class set the integral is Σ_h w_h θ_{P_h}/Σ_h w_h with inverse stabilizer weights. At sufficiently small level with equal stabilizer volumes this is c_K⁻¹Σ_hθ_{P_h}. One has E_{F,k}(τ)=Σ_{β∈P¹(F)}c(β,τ)^(−k), c(∞,τ)=1 and c(β,τ)=A_β Nm(τ+β), where A_β=Nm(c)/Nm(a) for Oc+Od=a and β=d/c; even k removes sign choices. Direct sums give θ_{P^ℓ}=θ_P^ℓ but not E_{P^ℓ}=E_P^ℓ.
items.note: Bogo–Li primary §2 read. Use rank at least 8, or increase a direct-sum power, whenever an absolutely convergent Eisenstein series is used in Lemmas 3.2–3.3. The mass convention is essential, E19.

items.name: Eisenstein series of I(s, χ) and the Siegel–Weil formula in signature (n, 2)
items.statement: For V of signature ((n, 2), (n+2, 0), …), the map λ(φ)(g) = (ω(g)φ)(0) gives standard sections of I(s_0, χ_V), s_0 = n/2, and E_L(τ, κ̃) = Σ_μ E(τ, φ_μ, κ̃) φ_μ with E(τ, φ_f, κ̃) = v^{−κ̃/2} E(g_τ, s_0, λ(φ_f) ⊗ Φ^κ̃_∞). For K fixing L̂ and acting trivially on L̂′/L̂: E_L(τ, κ̃) = vol(X_K)^{−1} ∫_{X_K} Θ_L(τ, z, h) Ω^n for n ≥ 1 (Bruinier–Yang 2011, Lemma 4.3), and E_L = 2 vol(X_K)^{−1} Σ_{[z,h]∈X_K} Θ_L(τ, z, h) for n = 0. Require the convergence hypotheses of Bruinier–Yang §4: V anisotropic over F or Witt rank(V)<n. For n=0 the sum is weighted: each CM point has multiplicity 2/w_K, and vol(X_K)=4|E×\Ê×/K|/w_K. These are not unweighted counts.

items.name: Ample twisting by the exceptional ideal divisor
items.statement: For a blowup π of a Noetherian scheme in a coherent finite-type ideal, use the existing planned exceptional Cartier divisor D with O(−D)=O(1). For an ample invertible sheaf L on the base, the π-ample O(−D) tensored with π*L^k is ample for all sufficiently large k. Finite surjective normalization pulls back ample sheaves to ample sheaves. Keep the multiplicities of D when comparing with the reduced boundary.
items.note: Import blowups and the exceptional-divisor identification from upstream StableReduction Layer 4, and relative Proj/ampleness from Layer 2. R09.1 supplies the remaining general Noetherian twist comparison; no new blowup carrier is proposed.

items.name: Automorphic and higher Green functions on orthogonal Shimura varieties
items.statement: For V/Q of signature (n,2), σ₀=n/4−1/2, m>0 in Z+Q(μ), define Φ_{m,μ}=2Γ(s+σ₀)/Γ(2s) times the sum over λ∈h(L_{m,μ}) of (m/Q(λ_z⊥))^(s+σ₀) F(s+σ₀,s−σ₀,2s;m/Q(λ_z⊥)). It converges normally off Z(m,μ) for Re(s)>σ₀+1. For r>0 and f with principal coefficients c(m,μ), choose the BEY normalization Φ^r=(r!/2)Σc(m,μ)m^r Φ_{m,μ}(σ₀+1+r), equal to (4π)^(-r) times the regularized lift of R^r f. For L=M₂(Z), Φ_m(r+1)=−2G^m_{r+1}/r!, so Φ^r=−G_{r+1,f}. The printed Li (3.29) is twice this normalization. An unsubtracted truncated integral is used only after proving its logarithmic divergence coefficient vanishes; otherwise take the regularized finite part. Ordinary evaluations exclude the singular divisor.
items.note: E15 corrects the individual Green scalar and E21 the finite-sum normalization. BEY Proposition 4.7 and (5.1) determine the factor one half; §5.1 determines the finite-part subtraction. Use one convention throughout the averages and Galois formulas; G3 retains the remaining convergence/application check.

items.name: Orthogonal GSpin datum and its negative-plane domain
items.statement: For a nondegenerate F-quadratic space of even dimension n+2 with signatures ((n,2),(n+2,0),...), form H=Res_{F/Q}GSpin(V), its central F× and spinor norm. The domain D is the two orientations of negative 2-planes at the distinguished real place, identified with the isotropic quadric {(Z,Z)=0,(Z,conj Z)<0} and, when the chosen isotropic pair exists, the tube domain z↦z+a−Q(z)b. X_K(C)=H(Q)\D×H(A_f)/K has dimension n and is projective if V is anisotropic. Generic Shimura quotient/canonical-model machinery is imported; the quadratic-datum specialization and comparisons are the new work.
items.note: Components, neighbors and modular-form bundles are separated below. Reuse the existing Clifford algebra; no duplicate Clifford carrier. Read mathlib:CliffordAlgebra Q: quotient of TensorAlgebra by ι(v)²=Q(v), over a commutative ring and module; it already has its ring and R-algebra structures. This does not define GSpin.

items.name: Example 2.7: Z(W_Q) is defined over Q for pairs of CM points on X_0(1)²
items.statement: For negative discriminants d_1, d_2 with F = Q(√(d_1d_2)) real quadratic, E = E_1E_2 is a CM extension of F and, as W with Q(μ) = −Nμμ̄/√D, the CM 0-cycle is Z(W) = Σ_{(σ_1,σ_2)∈G_1×G_2, σ_1|H_0 = σ_2|H_0} (z_1^{σ_1}, z_2^{σ_2}) + (−z̄_1^{σ_1}, −z̄_2^{σ_2}) with H_0 = H_1 ∩ H_2. Since every element of Gal(H_0/Q) has order dividing 2 (Li, Compositio 2021, Lemma 3.2), Z(W_Q) = Z(W(2)_Q) is defined over Q.
items.note: Requires distinct imaginary quadratic fields. The intersection-of-ring-class-fields input is Li 2021 Lemma 3.2, still a separately cited supplier. No claim of full reading of that paper.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: algebraicity of higher Green functions at an individual CM point on X_0(1)²
items.statement: Let r ∈ Z_{>0} and f ∈ M^!_{−2r} with integral Fourier coefficients, d_1, d_2 negative discriminants with one of them fundamental when r is odd, and z_i CM points of discriminant d_i with (z₁,z₂) outside the support of Z_f=Σ_{m>0}c(−m)m^r T_m. Then there are κ ∈ Z_{>0} (depending on d_1, d_2, r, f) and α = α(z_1, z_2) ∈ H^×, H = H_1H_2 (H_i the ring class field of E_i = Q(√d_i) for z_i) with (d_1d_2)^{r/2} G_{r+1,f}(z_1, z_2) = κ^{−1} log|α| and α(z_1^σ, z_2^σ) = σ(α(z_1, z_2)) for σ ∈ Gal(H/E_1E_2) (Remark 1.2: Gal(H/E) ⊂ Gal(H_1/E_1) × Gal(H_2/E_2)). This answers Zagier's ICM 1986 problem (ii) and the Gross–Zagier conjecture (4.4).
items.locator: Theorem 1.1, p. 377; Remark 1.2; proof in §5.3, p. 416, as completed by E8
items.note: Add the nonsingularity hypothesis, E12. Same-field case: BEY Theorem 6.1 followed by a norm from H_D to H₁H₂ and rational rescaling; do not assume these fields coincide. Distinct-field proof remains conditional on G1/G3.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: differences of higher Green functions at big CM points
items.statement: Let r∈Z_{>0} and V/Q have signature (n, 2), L ⊂ V even, f ∈ M^!_{1−n/2−2r, ρ̄_L} with integral Fourier coefficients, F totally real of degree d, and W an F-quadratic space from a CM extension E/F of signature ((0, 2), (2, 0), …) with W_Q ↪ V (so n + 2 ≥ 2d). Then there are λ_j ∈ F and α_j ∈ (E^ab)^× (1 ≤ j ≤ d) with Φ^r_L(z_0, h_1, f) − Φ^r_L(z_0, h_2, f) = Σ_j λ_j log|σ_{h_1}(α_j)/σ_{h_2}(α_j)| for all (z_0, h_i) ∈ Z(W_Q), σ_h ∈ Gal(E^ab/E) the class-field-theory image of h. If F = Q(√D) and n + 2 = 2d = 4, one may take λ_1 = D^{r/2}/κ (κ ∈ N) and λ_2 = 0. Remark 1.5: this holds even when Z(W_Q) meets the singularity of Φ^r_L, using the real-analytic continuation of Φ^r(z, 1, f) − Φ^r(z, h, f).
items.locator: Theorem 1.3, p. 378; Remark 1.5; proof in §5.1, pp. 414–415
items.note: The first result with n ≥ 3 and d ≥ 2. The proof reduces to L = N_0 via Lemma 2.2, uses Proposition 3.4, Theorem 4.3 and the operator 𝒟, then Theorem 4.10.

items.name: Theorem 1.7 with corrected dimension
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 1.3, assume F is real quadratic, n=2, r is positive and even, the singular divisor misses Z(W_Q), and Z(W_Q) is defined over Q. Then Conjecture 1.6 holds with λ₁∈Q and λ₂=0.

items.name: Small-CM algebraicity and the same-field modular-curve case
items.statement: Import BEY Theorem 5.5/Corollary 5.6 for weakly holomorphic input with integral coefficients and disjoint special divisor and small CM cycle. The normalized value is a logarithm of an element of the appropriate ring class field, equivariant under Artin reciprocity. In the modular-curve same-field case, BEY Theorem 6.1 gives |D|^r G_{r+1,f}(z₁^σ,z₂^σ)=−t⁻¹log|α^σ| with D=lcm(t₁,t₂)²D₀, d_i=t_i²D₀, α∈H_D× and t>0 depending only on D. Retain the nonsingularity restriction when ordinary values are intended.
items.note: BEY statements and their proof references were read. Coalesce with PAPER-BRUINIER-EHLEN-YANG-21 items 31,33. This is no longer a paper awaiting extraction.

items.name: Real-analytic Hilbert modular forms and Petersson pairing
items.statement: For a congruence Γ⊂SL₂(O_F), a finite-dimensional unitary representation ρ and κ∈Z^d, A_{κ,ρ}(Γ) is the space of real-analytic functions on H^d satisfying the slash transformation and boundedness near each cusp. Define κ̃=(−k₁,k₂,...), κ̂=(2−k₁,k₂,...), Petersson norm squared ⟨f,f⟩Nm(v^κ), and (f,g)_Pet=D_F^(−1/2)∫_{Γ\H^d}⟨f,g⟩Nm(v^κ)dμ when at least one input decays exponentially. Boundedness is not smooth extendability across a toroidal cusp.
items.note: Import the holomorphic/cuspidal subspaces from AutomorphicBundles B4. This item adds the real-analytic coefficient/growth interface, not a new classical Hilbert carrier.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: products of iterated raises span raised Rankin–Cohen brackets
items.statement: For real-analytic f,g:H→C, k,ℓ∈Q and r≥0, assume k+ℓ∉{−2r+2,...,0}, with the set empty for r=0. There exist rational c_{r,a,j} for 0≤a,j≤r such that R̃_k^a f·R̃_ℓ^(r−a)g=Σ_{j=0}^r c_{r,a,j}R̃_{k+ℓ+2j}^(r−j)[f,g]_j. Raising is iterated with the weight increasing by 2 at each step.
items.note: Checked the induction: the extra row has Σ c_a(−1)^a = C(k+ℓ+2r, r+1) ≠ 0.

items.name: Example 2.1: Rankin–Cohen brackets of exponentials and Legendre polynomials
items.statement: For κ = (1, 1), f = e(α_1τ_1 + α_2τ_2), α ∈ Q(√D) with tr α ≠ 0: e(−tr(α)τ)𝒞_{κ,r}(f)(τ) = Σ_s C(r, s)² α_1^{r−s}(−α_2)^s = tr(α)^r P_r(x), x = √D tr(α/√D)/tr(α), with P_r the r-th Legendre polynomial (parity (−1)^r; Rodrigues' formula).
items.note: Checked the algebra. Mathlib has no Legendre polynomials.

items.name: Corrected quotient-harmonic lowering identity
items.statement: For κ∈Z^d, r≥0 and holomorphic g not identically zero, let u=f/g on {g≠0}. Assume u is harmonic in τ₁ of weight k₁ and holomorphic in the other variables. Use the first-variable-first Cohen operator C¹_{κ,r}=C_{(k₁,trκ−k₁),r}(u(τ₁,τ′,...,τ′)). Then D_{κ,r}(f,g)=(g^Δ)^(r+1)C¹_{κ,r}(u) satisfies Lτ D=binom(k₁+r−1,r)(g^Δ)^(r+1)R̃_{trκ−2}^r((L_{τ₁}f)/g)^Δ wherever g^Δ≠0. Interpret D by its denominator-cleared differential polynomial across zeros and extend the identity whenever its right side also extends.
items.note: The original hypothesis on f is insufficient; require harmonicity of f/g. In §5.1, R_{τ₁,−1}(θ_N−θ_N(h))=0 proves the required quotient condition off G=0. This does not by itself settle the integral-normalization or boundary gaps.

items.name: Kronecker's approximation theorem and Lemma 2.8
items.statement: (Kronecker) if 1, θ_1, …, θ_N are Q-linearly independent, the points (nθ_j mod 1)_j, n ∈ N, are dense in (R/Z)^N. Lemma 2.8: for such θ_j, M ∈ Z_{>0} and 0 ≤ b < M, and any α_j ∈ R, there is an infinite sequence n_i with e((Mn_i + b)θ_j) → e(α_j) for all j.
items.locator: Lemma 2.8, p. 394; statement as corrected by E1
items.note: Kronecker's theorem (Apostol, Thm. 7.10) is not in Mathlib or the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 2.9, Remark 2.10 and Corollary 2.11: vanishing of exponential sums
items.statement: Let α_i, c_i ∈ C with an integer s₀>0 and Σ α_i c_i^{s₀} absolutely convergent and, for every ε > 0, only finitely many i with |c_i| ≥ ε. If φ(s) = Σ α_i c_i^s vanishes for all but finitely many s ∈ Z_{>s_0}, then Σ_{c_i = c} α_i = 0 for every c ∈ C^×, so φ(s)=0 throughout its positive-integer convergence range (Lemma 2.9); if moreover all α_i > 0 then all c_i = 0 (Remark 2.10, strengthening Freitag's Lemma 5.6_1). Corollary 2.11: if Σ c_i^s and Σ b_j^s converge absolutely at s_0 > 0 and agree for all but finitely many s ∈ Z_{>s_0}, the non-zero c_i and b_j correspond bijectively.
items.locator: Lemma 2.9, p. 394; Remark 2.10, p. 394; Corollary 2.11, p. 396; statement as corrected by E2
items.note: As printed Lemma 2.9 has no condition on the moduli |c_i| and is false (E2). The added condition holds automatically in Corollary 2.11 (s_0 > 0) and in Lemmas 3.2–3.3.

items.name: Lemma 3.2: Eisenstein nonvanishing on a finite set
items.statement: For P∈U_F⁺ and a finite set S⊂H^d, there is ℓ≥1 such that E_{P^ℓ} is nonzero at every point of S. Work with a sufficiently large direct-sum power to place all Eisenstein sums in the absolute convergence range; eventual vanishing of all products over S contradicts corrected Remark 2.10 and the all-∞ term.
items.locator: Lemma 3.2; Lemma 3.3, p. 400; proofs as corrected by E3–E4
items.note: Correct reciprocal bases and quantification, E3. Lemma 3.3 is separated below; E4 is its normalization slip.

items.name: Proposition 3.4: partition of unity on the diagonal
items.statement: There are m ∈ N and P̃_i, P_{1,i}, P_{2,i} ∈ U_F^+ (ranks 2𝔯̃_i, 2𝔯_i, P_{1,i} and P_{2,i} in the same genus) such that the (E_{P̃_i}(θ_{P_{1,i}} − θ_{P_{2,i}}))^Δ have no common zero on H; hence for any d_i, e_i ∈ N there are g_i ∈ M^!_{−(𝔯̃_i d_i + 𝔯_i e_i)d} with rational Fourier coefficients and Σ_i g_i (E^{d_i}_{P̃_i}(θ_{P_{1,i}} − θ_{P_{2,i}})^{e_i})^Δ = 1.
items.note: Checked: Δ^{−(…)d}(E^{12d_i}(θ−θ)^{12e_i})^Δ = A_i(j) ∈ Q[j] with gcd(A_i) = 1, and g_i := B_i(j)Δ^{−(…)d}(E^{11d_i}(θ−θ)^{11e_i})^Δ.

items.name: Theorem 4.1: surjectivity of ∂̄ after twisting by an ample boundary bundle
items.statement: Let X = Γ\H^d (Γ neat), X̃ a smooth toroidal compactification from a projective admissible decomposition, L̃_{κ,ρ} the extended sheaves of modular forms. For every N there are n_0, k > N such that H⁰(X̃, E^{0,0} ⊗ L̃_{κ,ρ} ⊗ L̃_{k⃗}(−D)^{⊗n}) → H⁰(X̃, E′ ⊗ L̃_{κ,ρ} ⊗ L̃_{k⃗}(−D)^{⊗n}) (∂̄ ⊗ 1 ⊗ 1) is surjective for all n ≥ n_0, with L̃_{κ,ρ} locally free on the smooth toroidal compactification, where D is the exceptional Cartier divisor of the blow-up (supported on the boundary E).
items.locator: Theorem 4.1; proof pp. 403–404, as corrected by E6
items.note: Use an actual holomorphic vector bundle F on the smooth compactification and the ample twist A=O(−D)⊗π*L^k. GAGA/Serre vanishing applies to F⊗A^n. Do not infer the required smooth boundary section from boundedness of the original automorphic function (G1/E17).

items.name: Proposition 4.2: L_{τ_1}-preimages of g^ℓ f
items.statement: For f ∈ A_{κ̃,ρ}(Γ) holomorphic in τ_2, …, τ_d and g ∈ S_{κ′}(Γ) of parallel weight, there are ℓ_0 and Ĝ_ℓ ∈ A_{κ̂+ℓκ′,ρ}(Γ) for ℓ ≥ ℓ_0, holomorphic in τ_2, …, τ_d, with L_{τ_1}Ĝ_ℓ = g^ℓ f and Ĝ_{ℓ′} = g^{ℓ′−ℓ}Ĝ_ℓ. For the proof recorded here, additionally require that v₁⁻²g^{ℓ₀}f dconj(τ₁) extends as the required smooth closed bundle-valued form on the compactification. The claimed result for every bounded real-analytic f is a separate unresolved target, G1.
items.note: Weighted divisor repair: choose k>k′ max a_σ, then ℓ₀=n₀k and twist exponent n=n₀k′ give ℓ₀E≥nD with matching weights. A numerical vanishing order is not by itself C∞ extension; E17.

items.name: Theorem 4.3 and Remark 4.4: the real-analytic Hilbert modular forms δ̂
items.statement: Let W be an F-quadratic space of dimension 2 and signature ((0, 2), (2, 0), …), P_1, P_2 ∈ U_F^+ of rank 2𝔯 in the same genus, N ⊂ W an O-lattice. There is ℓ_0 such that for all ℓ ≥ ℓ_0 and h ∈ H_W(Q̂) there is δ̂ = δ̂(τ; N, h, P_1, P_2, ℓ) ∈ A_{1+ℓ𝔯, ρ_N} (parallel weight) that (1) is holomorphic in τ_2, …, τ_d with exponential decay at the cusps; (2) satisfies L_{τ_1}δ̂ = (θ_{P_1} − θ_{P_2})^ℓ(θ_N(τ) − θ_N(τ, h)); (3) equals δ̂^+ + (θ_{P_1} − θ_{P_2})^ℓ(θ*_N(τ) − θ*_N(τ, h)) with δ̂^+ holomorphic and Γ_∞-invariant; (4) has â^+_{m,μ} = 0 unless m ≫ 0 and lim_{v_1→∞} â_{m,μ}(v_1) = â^+_{m,μ}; (5) satisfies lim_{|v|→∞} ∂^{r_1}_{τ_1}⋯∂^{r_d}_{τ_d}(δ̂ − δ̂^+) = 0. Remark 4.4: δ̂^+ is unique up to cusp forms of parallel weight 𝔯ℓ + 1.
items.locator: Theorem 4.3; Remark 4.4, p. 405; statement as corrected by E5
items.note: Target with a recorded proof gap G1: establish the required boundary regularity for the actual theta data, or supply an appropriate weighted ∂̄ argument. Parts (1)–(5), decay under differentiation and holomorphic ambiguity must be proved separately in the blueprint.

items.name: Harmonic Whittaker forms and principal parts
items.statement: For d≥2, an even O_F-lattice L of signature ((n,2),(n+2,0),...) with n>2, put s₀=n/2 and κ=(1−s₀,s₀+1,...). The basis function f_{m,μ}, for m≫0 in d_F⁻¹+Q(μ), is Nm(4πm)^s₀/((4πm₁)^s₀ Γ(s₀)^d) times (Γ(s₀)−Γ(s₀,4πm₁v₁)) exp(4πm₁v₁)e(−tr(m conj τ))φ_μ. H_{κ,conj ρ_L} is its finite linear span. The principal-part map sends f_{m,μ} to q^(−m)φ_μ and is an isomorphism onto the finite principal-part space. These functions are not ordinary holomorphic modular forms.
items.note: The totally real Whittaker carrier is not the elliptic Maass carrier of QM.3.

items.name: Borcherds product for weakly holomorphic Whittaker input
items.statement: For d≥2,n>2 and f∈M!_{κ,conj ρ_L} with integral principal-part coefficients, Bruinier Theorem 6.8 constructs a meromorphic modular form Ψ_L of weight −B(f), divisor Z(f), and finite-order unitary multiplier, with −log‖Ψ_L‖²_Pet=Φ_L. After killing the multiplier and descending the line bundle and divisor, write Φ_L=2log|C_L|−(2/M)log‖R_L‖_Pet with R_L defined over σ₁(F) and C_L constant on connected components. This does not hold for arbitrary harmonic Whittaker input with ξ(f)≠0.
items.locator: §4.4, (4.29)–(4.30), pp. 411–412; Bruinier Theorem 6.8, author manuscript pp. 35–36
items.note: Correct an extraction omission: integrality alone did not imply ξ(f)=0. Bruinier Theorem 6.8 and proof were read; finite-order multipliers use Margulis for n>2, and lower-dimensional embedding arguments in the more general source.

items.name: Lemma 4.5: differences of theta lifts are real-analytic across the singularity
items.statement: Let n>2, z₀∈D, S=V(F)∩z₀⊥, and h₀,h₀′∈H(A_f). Assume h₀⁻¹|_S=h₀′⁻¹|_S (or directly equality, with weights, of the rational norm-index vectors in h₀(L+μ)∩S and h₀′(L+μ)∩S for every principal-part index). Then the logarithmic singularities cancel in Φ_L(z,h₀,f)−Φ_L(z,h₀′,f). The difference extends real-analytically near z₀, and its normalized difference integral converges there after removing the common singular terms.
items.note: Equality of the forward maps on S is insufficient. The application h₀=1,h₀′=h_W fixes S pointwise, so satisfies the corrected inverse criterion. No punctured neighborhood removes a positive-dimensional divisor; work with cancellation along the entire local divisor.

items.name: Lemma 4.6 and Remark 4.7: Stokes for the regularized theta integral
items.statement: Let n = 2s_0 > 2, f = Σ c(m, μ)f_{m,μ} ∈ H_{κ,ρ̄_L}, η ∈ A_{κ̃,ρ_L} with convergent regularized pairing, and η̂ = Σ b̂_{m,μ}(v_1)e(tr(mτ))φ_μ ∈ A_{κ̂,ρ_L} with L_{τ_1}η̂ = η and ‖η̂‖_Pet bounded. Then D_F^(−1/2)∫^reg⟨f, η̄⟩(v_2⋯v_d)^{s_0+1}dμ = −(η̂, ξ(f))_Pet + lim_{T→∞}Σ c(m, μ) b̂_{m,μ}(T); the limit exists (Remark 4.7).
items.note: Restore D_F^(−1/2), E14. The lower endpoint is O(t^((s₀−1)/2)); this tends to zero because n>2. Use the finite coefficient pairing, not an unjustified exchange of an infinite principal part.

items.name: Proposition 4.8 and Remark 4.9: the pairing identity
items.statement: With L_i = N ⊕ P̃ ⊕ P_1^i ⊕ P_2^{ℓ−i}, V = Ũ ⊕ U ⊕ W, η̂_P̃ = θ_P̃ δ̂ and η̂^+_P̃ = θ_P̃ δ̂^+: Σ_{0≤i≤ℓ}(−1)^{ℓ−i}C(ℓ, i)(Φ_{L_i}(z_0, 1, f) − Φ_{L_i}(z_0, h_W, f)) = −(η̂_P̃, ξ(f))_Pet + {η̂^+_P̃, f} for every f ∈ H_{κ,ρ̄_N}; the same holds with P̃ replaced by P̃_h̃, h̃ ∈ H_Ũ(Q̂) (Remark 4.9).
items.note: Use the corrected inverse-action lemma, discriminant-normalized Stokes identity, and the binomial expansion. The coefficient at the final boundary is that of η̂, not the earlier δ̂ alone. G1 remains upstream.

items.name: Theorem 4.10 and Remark 4.11: algebraicity of the pairing with E_P̃ δ̂^+
items.statement: For weakly holomorphic f = f_𝒫 ∈ M^!_{κ,ρ̄_N} with coefficients in a number field 𝔽 ⊂ C, there are λ_1, …, λ_m ∈ 𝔽 and α_1, …, α_m ∈ E_W^ab, independent of h_W, with {E_P̃ δ̂^+, 𝒫} = Σ_i λ_i log|α_i/σ(α_i)|, where σ ∈ Gal(E_W^ab/E_W) corresponds to h_W ∈ H_W(Q̂) ≅ Ê_W^×. One can take m ≤ [𝔽 : Q]; the denominators of the λ_i depend on f through the multiplier order (Remark 4.11).
items.note: Read the proof and checked cancellation and the binomial sign, E9. Choose sufficiently small level (or account for stabilizer weights) for the finite product averaging. The normalized Borcherds input is weakly holomorphic, and G1 remains upstream.

items.name: Singular theta primitive
items.statement: For q₁≥1 use φ*(τ,z,λ)=−e(Q(λ)τ)(−4πQ(λ_z))^(1−q₁/2) Γ(q₁/2−1,−4πQ(λ_z)v) when λ∉z⊥, and e(Q(λ)τ)CT_{s=0} v^(s+q₁/2−1)/(s+q₁/2−1) when λ∈z⊥. Its lattice sum Θ*_L converges, satisfies L_{τ₁}Θ*_L=Θ_L, and need not be modular. For negative binary N the zero term is log(v₁)φ₀ and cancels in θ*_N−θ*_N(h).

items.name: Serre vanishing and analytic comparison
items.statement: For a projective complex scheme, an ample invertible sheaf A and a coherent sheaf F, H^i(F⊗A^n)=0 for i>0 and n sufficiently large. Projective GAGA transfers this to coherent analytic cohomology.

items.name: The different has square ideal class
items.statement: For a number field F, the class of its different in Cl(F) is a square. Choose a fractional ideal a and δ∈F× with d_F⁻¹=a²(δ); after clearing denominators a can be taken integral.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6 proof, p. 391; Weil, Basic Number Theory, last cited theorem
items.note: Quoted input, not independently read in Weil. G2 retains the full proof acquisition.

items.name: Convergence, eigenvalue and continuation of orthogonal Green functions
items.statement: For m>0 and σ₀=n/4−1/2, the hypergeometric Green series converges normally off Z(m,μ) for Re(s)>σ₀+1 and has Laplace eigenvalue (s−σ₀−1)(s+σ₀)/2. Its meromorphic continuation has a simple pole at s=σ₀+1; the constant term gives the ordinary regularized Green function. Keep spectral continuation, singularity analysis and the raising-lift comparison as distinct proof tasks. The regularized higher lift is (r!/2)Σc(m,μ)m^rΦ_{m,μ}, since the normalized Poincaré series has both μ and −μ principal terms.
items.note: Shared with BEY extraction items 27–28, not a second construction. Only the unit-disc hypergeometric function itself is in Mathlib.

items.name: Spinor-norm description of components
items.statement: For the orthogonal Shimura datum of §2.3 with n>0, identify π₀(X_K) with H(Q)⁺\H(A_f)/K and then F₊×\Â_F×/ν(K); fix the class-field extension E_K/F and the inverse-Artin convention determining the component Y_K^σ. For n=0 use the separate CM torus double quotient with two orientations.

items.name: Neighboring quadratic spaces and conjugate Shimura varieties
items.statement: Given the admissible incoherent totally positive adelic quadratic space, its real-place neighbors V(j) have signature (n,2) at j and are positive at the other real places, with fixed finite-place identifications. Their canonical varieties are the conjugates of a single F-variety; as a Q-scheme its complex points are their disjoint union.
items.locator: §2.3, p. 390; Bruinier–Yang §7, Lemma 7.1, author manuscript p. 38

items.name: Meromorphic orthogonal modular forms and Petersson norm
items.statement: For the chosen tube-domain automorphy factor j(γ,z), a weight-w meromorphic modular form Ψ(z,h) is right K-invariant and satisfies Ψ(γz,γh)=j(γ,z)^w Ψ(z,h), with the prescribed boundary behavior. Its invariant norm is |Ψ(z,h)| |Im z|^w; fix the metric before interpreting −log‖Ψ‖².

Track stack/stabilizer multiplicities. For φ_μ write Z(m,μ); for a finite Whittaker principal part define Z(f)=Σc(m,μ)Z(m,μ).

items.name: Conjecture 1.6 as an unproved target statement
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 1.3 and away from the singular divisor, ask for λ_j∈F and α_j∈E^ab such that Φ^r_L(z₀,h,f)=Σ_j λ_j log|σ_h(α_j)| simultaneously on the CM cycle. This item records a conjecture, not a proved theorem; Li proves only the specified cases.

items.name: Full big-CM average for a real quadratic field
items.statement: For V=Res_{F/Q}W of signature (2,2), BEY Theorem 5.10 pairs a harmonic input with the Cohen operator applied to the holomorphic derivative of the incoherent Eisenstein series, with a shadow correction. For weakly holomorphic input the shadow term vanishes. When r is even and the two conjugate CM cycles agree, it gives (2/deg Z(W_Q))Φ^r_L(Z(W_Q),f)=CT⟨f,C_{(1,1),r}(E_L⁺)⟩ in the BEY convention. This is the corrected BEY-compatible convention of item 15. For the printed Li (3.29), multiply the entire value by 2; G3 retains the convergence check in the application.

items.name: Odd-weight partial CM average
items.statement: Use BEY Theorem 7.13 and Corollary 7.15, or its introduction Theorem 1.2: for distinct imaginary quadratic fields and d₁ fundamental, the normalized partial average over the CM divisor of discriminant d₁ is t⁻¹log|α^σ| with α∈H_{d₂}(√d₁) for odd r and σ fixing Q(√d₁,√d₂). Retain CM-divisor weights and the Galois subgroup of the actual partial orbit.
items.note: The introduction statement was read; exact §7 constants are a coalesced BEY obligation, not re-proved here.

items.name: Logarithmic Fourier coefficients of the incoherent derivative
items.statement: BKY Proposition 4.6 and its local proof express the positive Fourier coefficients of the holomorphic part of the normalized incoherent Eisenstein derivative as finite linear combinations of log p with coefficients in the field generated by the finite Schwartz function. In particular rational Schwartz data give rational logarithmic coefficients. Keep the rational factor Λ(0,χ), the constant term and the nonholomorphic negative-index terms separate.
items.locator: Li §5.2, pp. 415–416; BKY author manuscript Proposition 4.6, pp. 18–21

items.name: Legendre polynomial used by the Cohen coefficient
items.statement: For r≥0 define P_r(X)=(2^r r!)⁻¹(d/dX)^r(X²−1)^r in Q[X]. Its binomial expression is 2^(−r)Σ_s binom(r,s)²(X+1)^(r−s)(X−1)^s, with P_r(−X)=(−1)^rP_r(X).

items.name: Lemma 3.3: a same-genus theta difference is nonzero at a prescribed point
items.statement: For every τ₀∈H^d there exist P₁,P₂∈U_F⁺ of the same rank and genus with θ_{P₁}(τ₀)≠θ_{P₂}(τ₀). If all same-genus values were equal, mass-normalized Siegel–Weil would imply E_{P^ℓ}(τ₀)=E_P(τ₀)^ℓ. The corrected exponential-sum uniqueness would identify infinitely many nonzero Hecke bases with a singleton, a contradiction.

items.statement: At full level, the rational Fourier-coefficient weight-zero weakly holomorphic forms are Q[j]; Δ is a nowhere-zero cusp form on H of weight 12. Therefore the weight-zero forms Δ^(−wd)(E_P^(12a)(θ₁−θ₂)^(12b))^Δ are polynomials A_i(j), and absence of common zeros implies gcd(A_i)=1 in Q[j]. Bezout gives the precise rational partition in Proposition 3.4.

This intertwines the Weil representation, preserves rational/integral principal parts, and preserves the theta pairing and higher lift with the correct normalization. Apply it before replacing L by L̃⊕Res N.
items.note: The discriminant-module map is not an equality of the two lattices. Coalesce with BEY item 23.

items.name: Descent of equivariant logarithms by a field norm
items.statement: Let M/H/E be finite abelian extensions and a∈M×. Suppose log|σ(a)| is constant on each Gal(M/H)-coset. Then b=Norm_{M/H}(a)∈H× satisfies log|σ(b)|=[M:H]log|σ(a)|. This gives the desired smaller class field after adjusting the common rational denominator. For finitely many CM values whose differences are equivariant logarithms and whose weighted sum is log of a rational number, solve the finite system after passing to a common finite abelian extension and clearing stabilizer and orbit multiplicities.

items.name: The quotient in the main proof is harmonic
items.statement: With η̂=E_P̃ δ̂ and G=E_P̃(θ_{P₁}−θ_{P₂})^ℓ, on G≠0 one has L₁(η̂/G)=θ_N−θ_N(h). Each negative-binary theta summand is v₁ times an antiholomorphic exponential in τ₁, hence R_{−1}θ_N=0. Thus Δ₁(η̂/G)=0 at weight 1; the quotient is holomorphic in the remaining variables. Apply corrected Lemma 2.3 and then the polynomial extension across G=0.

items.name: Finite principal part adjoint to the Hilbert differential operator
items.statement: For weakly holomorphic elliptic f₀g of weight 2−k and the polynomial operator D_{1,r}, construct the finite Hilbert principal part P_r over F satisfying {f₀g,D_{1,r}(δ,G)}={P_r,δ} on Fourier series supported on totally positive indices. Finiteness uses the finite negative elliptic principal part and finiteness of totally positive lattice indices with bounded trace. If δ is a Hilbert cusp form its image is an elliptic cusp form, and the weight-two constant-term residue theorem forces the pairing to vanish; hence P_r corresponds to a weakly holomorphic Whittaker form.
items.note: This is a substantive construction omitted from the original extraction. Preserve the totally positive support and residue theorem; arbitrary formal series do not automatically have a well-defined infinite diagonal coefficient.

routes.title: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights, Part II: CM values of higher Green functions on orthogonal Shimura varieties
routes.brief:
First prerequisite: Gross–Zagier formulas and arithmetic heights (GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights). Maintain exactly one HigherGreenFunctionCMValues Part II coordinated with PAPER-BRUINIER-EHLEN-YANG-21 route 6, which already exists as an extraction. This review does not approve launching a second design or treating unreviewed BEY items as implemented declarations.

Final targets are corrected Li Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.7 in items 19–21, with the off-singular-divisor hypothesis for individual values, n=2 in Theorem 1.7, and the class-field norm descent for the same-field case. Conjecture 1.6 is only a recorded conjecture. The proof plan must first discharge G1 (boundary regularity) and G3 (normalizations); the full Li target is not a theorem supplied by a corrected-looking formula alone.

Construct the quadratic GSpin datum, oriented domain, connected components, neighboring varieties, special/CM cycles with stabilizer multiplicities, and modular forms with their Petersson metric. Import generic Shimura data/canonical models from ShimuraVarieties V2/V4/V6, compactifications from ShimuraCompactifications C2/C6 and automorphic bundles/classical Hilbert forms from AutomorphicBundles B3/B4. Coordinate the ordinary Green and special-divisor carriers with GSpinSpecialDivisorHeights and BEY items 27–29. Import the elliptic Maass carrier and raising/lowering operators from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3, and the Weil representation and ordinary theta kernels from MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.4–MP.5. The nonmodular singular theta primitive, incomplete Gamma estimates, real-analytic Hilbert growth space and totally real harmonic Whittaker carrier are additional constructions.

The elementary operator spine consists of Rankin–Cohen operators, Lemma 2.2, Legendre polynomials and Example 2.1, the first-variable-first Hilbert operator, its polynomial extension across zeros, and corrected Lemma 2.3 with harmonicity of f/g. Prove separately that η̂/G is harmonic in the actual theta application. The nonvanishing spine uses Kronecker with 1 included in the independence hypothesis, the corrected exponential-sum uniqueness with bases tending to zero, Lemmas 3.2–3.3, and Proposition 3.4. Import the existing finite-zero theorem and holomorphic level-one ring; construct the weakly holomorphic localization and rational Q[j] comparison before the Bezout argument.

Use GN.2 for O_F-lattices and GN.3 for mass-normalized definite Siegel–Weil; MP.6 supplies the indefinite formula. Use upstream StableReduction Layers 2 and 4 for relative Proj, ampleness and blowups, then R09.1 for the general exceptional-ideal twist comparison and ComplexComparisonPartII C1/C2 for Dolbeault and Serre/GAGA. Prove the weighted boundary regularity needed by Proposition 4.2; bounded real-analytic forms do not automatically extend smoothly. Then prove each property of Theorem 4.3, including differentiated cusp decay, and its cusp-form ambiguity.

Separate the Whittaker principal-part isomorphism, ξ-surjectivity, weak kernel, rational Fourier structure and coefficient pairing. The Petersson identity has a cusp-form argument. Construct the regularized lift with D_F^(-1/2) and its prescribed order of integration. The Borcherds product requires ξ(f)=0 and integral coefficients. Correct Lemma 4.5 to inverse-action agreement; prove local cancellation along divisors. Derive the normalized Stokes formula, binomial pairing and Theorem 4.10 with sufficiently small level or explicit stabilizer weights, followed by the finite principal-part adjoint in §5.1. Import BEY small-CM/full-average/partial-average statements through the coordinated extraction and GZ.6’s incoherent derivative coefficients.

Tests include r=0,1 operator signs; f=log(v₁),g=exp(2πiτ₁) excluding the false Lemma 2.3; diagonal CM singularities excluded from Theorem 1.1; the p=5 forward-map counterexample to Lemma 4.5; normalized mass at fine and coarse level; scalar-extension and trace-dual examples; and the exact factors Φ_m/G_m=−2/r! and Φ^r=(r!/2)Σc m^rΦ_m from the hypergeometric series and BEY Poincaré normalization. These are planning tests, not Lean verification.

sourceIssues.printed: "Let θ1, …, θN ∈ R be Q-linearly independent irrational numbers, M ∈ N and b an integer with 0 ≤ b ≤ M − 1. For any α1, …, αN ∈ R, there exists an infinite subsequence {ni} ⊂ N such that lim e((Mni + b)θj) = e(αj) for all 1 ≤ j ≤ N."
sourceIssues.correction: Assume that 1, θ1, …, θN are Q-linearly independent.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the lemma is false. θ1 = √2 and θ2 = 1 − √2 are irrational and Q-linearly independent, but e(nθ1)e(nθ2) = 1 for every n, so (e(1/2), e(0)) is never approached. The proof cites Kronecker's theorem (Apostol, Thm. 7.10), which needs the stronger hypothesis. The only application, in the proof of Lemma 2.9, chooses θj with 1, θ1, …, θN linearly independent, so nothing downstream is affected.
